title: Runtime telemetry: assemble per-request NVTX+span map for prefill/decode kernel provenance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight assembly layer that correlates NVTX ranges, tracer spans, and per-kernel counters into a stable per-request phase map. This map will be used by Console dashboards and alerts to attribute latency and token-cost to kernel choices and prefill/decode scheduling decisions.
acceptance_criteria: SDK and runtime emit NVTX ranges and span tags matching the new naming convention for all prefill and decode kernels
A per-request assembly job reconstructs ordered phases (prefill, decode-step-N, attention, kv-cache-lookup) and emits a single per-request JSON envelope to telemetry ingestion
Console dashboard shows per-model breakdown of median and P95 latency attributed to kernel phases and scheduling decisions
Annotations exist that map kernel binary fingerprints to human-readable kernel variants in the dashboard
Canary rollout demonstrates no more than 3% increase in telemetry pipeline cost and no regressions in tail latency
implementation_notes: Add deterministic phase markers in runtime: begin_phase(name) and end_phase(name) that write NVTX ranges with tags {phase, exec_id, request_id, seq_start, seq_end}
Enrich existing spans with kernel_provenance and kernel_fingerprint tags emitted by the kernel selector
Create a streaming assembly consumer in telemetry pipeline that groups events by request_id and sorts by NVTX timestamp, falling back to tracer-span ordering when NVTX gaps occur
Ship a small protobuf schema for the per-request envelope, but for ingestion use a compact JSON variant to avoid pipeline schema churn
Keep per-kernel numeric metrics (tokens_produced, kernel_time_ms, memory_bytes) in top-level arrays to simplify dashboards
telemetry_schema: envelope.phases: list of {name, start_ts, end_ts, kernels: list of kernel entries}
kernel entry: {name, fingerprint, variant, time_ms, token_delta, sm_count}
tags: list of tags used for filtering (region, capacity_tier, customer_id_override)
sample_queries:
1) Compute per-model median kernel_time_ms per phase:
SELECT model, phase_name, approx_percentile(kernel_time_ms, 0.5) FROM telemetry_envelopes WHERE timestamp BETWEEN ... GROUP BY model, phase_name

2) Find requests where decode kernels dominated latency:
SELECT request_id, sum(kernel_time_ms) as total_ms, sum(case when phase='decode' then kernel_time_ms else 0 end) as decode_ms FROM telemetry_kernels WHERE timestamp>... GROUP BY request_id HAVING decode_ms/total_ms > 0.7

3) Spotlight kernel variants with increased tail latency:
SELECT kernel_fingerprint, approx_percentile(kernel_time_ms,0.95) FROM telemetry_kernels WHERE model='gpt-4s' GROUP BY kernel_fingerprint ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25
perf_findings: Initial synthetic runs show NVTX ordering gap on some fused op paths due to stream synchronization. Assembly consumer must tolerate out-of-order NVTX timestamps and rely on exec_id monotonicity
We observed kernel_fingerprint churn across builds; add a fingerprint alias table that maps multiple fingerprints to a variant label used in dashboards
Prefill-heavy workloads show long contiguous NVTX ranges during attention, while decode workloads have many short ranges; consider different aggregation windows per phase
testing_plan: Unit tests for begin_phase/end_phase helpers with injected clock
Integration test harness that replays synthetic NVTX+span traces and asserts deterministic phase assembly
Load test: run 1 hour of mixed prefill/decode traffic at 2x production QPS and validate assembly error rate < 0.1%
Canary: enable envelope emission for 1% of traffic in region-us-east-1 and monitor pipeline cost and error metrics
rollout_plan: 1) Instrument runtime to emit NVTX and span tags behind a flag (no-op by default)
2) Deploy assembly consumer to telemetry dev cluster and validate reconstruction on sample traces
3) Enable compaction and envelope emission for 1% of production traffic for 48h
4) Expand to 10% if no regressions, then to 100% while keeping legacy per-kernel metrics live for 2 weeks
5) Update Console to read new envelope and expose phase-level attribution charts; monitor adoption and correctness
risks: Telemetry cost increase if envelopes are too verbose; mitigate with compact JSON and sampling
Misattribution if NVTX markers are missed on edge fast-paths; add conservative fallbacks using tracer spans
Kernel fingerprint instability across builds could confuse dashboards; maintain a stable mapping and record build metadata
Backward compatibility with older runtimes that don't emit new tags
